correctness.rationale: Each generic intersected cube edge contributes exactly one section vertex; the hypercube graph has minimum cuts of size d only at singleton/complement singleton, proved inductively. The two extreme intercept intervals have lengths min_i(a_i|U_i|), the total width is sum_i(a_i|U_i|), and Gaussian radial cancellation produces the integral with exact normalization. Concavity of a minimum plus positive-probability branch-switching proves strict Schur concavity at fixed sum. Elementary halfnormal near-zero asymptotics give the pi/d² limit. All three-dimensional chamber sequences and spherical triangle boundary integrals were reconstructed; the independent standard-library checker exhaustively checks finite chamber cases and the analytic formulas. Finite sampling does not replace any infinite proof.

An exact simplex event law for every orthotope and d≥3, a strict cube rigidity theorem at fixed total edge lengths, a sharp high-dimensional decay constant pi, and a complete probability spectrum for affine 3-cube sections jointly answer a natural whole-family question, not an arbitrary example. Prior first moment is explicitly distinguished. The full vector is not a consequence of the one known mean.
